findings.expected: An ordinary chat skill invocation obeys its current Skills switch.
findings.changed: Ordinary local tool dispatch uses runLocalSkill and the same enabled-state gate as named skills.
findings.acceptance: With Notes Off, ordinary note search returns no note content; enable Notes and the same search can return the synthetic note.

findings.expected: Ordinary note-search grammar passes the requested query rather than the command prefix.
findings.changed: Extracts the search phrase after search [my] notes [for/about] before calling the note adapter.
findings.acceptance: The ordinary command search my notes SYNTHETIC_COBALT returns the note containing that marker without requiring the command prefix in its content.

findings.expected: A retry reads the current skill switch rather than a captured older value.
findings.changed: Skill dispatch reads enabledSkillsRef.current; the ref updates in a layout effect when preferences change.
remaining: The helper off/on branch is executed in fixtures; the actual ref-backed callback is source-reviewed.
findings.acceptance: Capture a failed Notes-Off request, turn Notes On, and retry through the same dispatcher; latest state is used and only one execution occurs.

findings.expected: Library deletion clearly distinguishes the retained historical attachment copy from the removed Library record.
findings.changed: Deletion confirmation discloses retained conversation/export copies and uses the tombstoned Library-delete helper; no historical messages are silently rewritten.
remaining: The full attach/send/delete/inspect-next-provider-context browser sequence remains unrun. The synthetic fixture verifies retained conversation text and Library deletion/tombstones. Stable cross-conversation attachment lineage remains a future extension.
findings.acceptance: Deleting a Library entry removes that record, leaves historical conversations intact, and explicitly tells the owner that previous attachments/exports may retain text.

findings.expected: Ordinary archive merge cannot resurrect a deliberately deleted Library ID.
findings.changed: Persists deletedFileIds tombstones through normalization, export and merge. Explicit replacement can restore a new identity while preserving tombstones.
findings.acceptance: Delete a synthetic file, export/reload, then merge an older archive: the old ID stays deleted. Explicit replacement creates a new restored ID.

findings.expected: Repeated identical attachments reuse capacity within their original project scope.
findings.changed: Deduplicates matching project/name/text/document metadata before enforcing the Library cap; changed revisions or other projects remain distinct.
findings.acceptance: Ten identical scoped attachments create one file; a different revision and another project each create a separate file.

findings.expected: Speak can use an independently selected text-answer provider with compatible separate input/output engines.
findings.changed: Added a turn-by-turn pipeline and selectors for local/cloud transcription, current selected answer route, browser/cloud/no speech output; xAI realtime remains an explicitly selected alternative.
remaining: Only synthetic provider receipts were exercised. No claim that Gemini or another live API actually answered. Local Handy/device availability and physical microphone behavior require later authorized verification.
findings.acceptance: Local input + Gemini-labelled synthetic answer + browser output completes with three distinct receipts and zero xAI calls; unavailable selected engines return clear errors without substitution.

findings.expected: Free-only mode allows local input and browser output while blocking chargeable speech stages before dispatch.
findings.changed: Stage-specific spending gates replace a blanket block; cloud transcription/speech remain unavailable in free-only mode and a completed answer is preserved if output is blocked.
findings.acceptance: Handy input/browser speech works in fixture free-only mode; selecting cloud input causes zero capture/provider calls, and blocked cloud output preserves the text answer.

findings.expected: An ended/replaced Speak call cannot play an older delayed response in the next call.
findings.changed: Call-generation and abort state bind capture, answer and playback to the current session. A late answer/mute change blocks speech generation or playback.
findings.acceptance: Finish call A/open B while A answers: A never speaks in B. Mute during answer latency preserves text and suppresses speech.

findings.expected: Speak attributes audio input, the actual answer turn and speech output separately.
findings.changed: Three-stage receipts and mode-specific labels replace one ambiguous provider label. Each answer uses its own delivery receipt; absent identity is shown as not reported.
findings.acceptance: A previous Gemini receipt cannot label the next response when its adapter supplies no identity; output/browser and realtime xAI labels remain distinct.

findings.expected: Existing bot chats show their saved configuration revision and apply newer settings only through an explicit action.
findings.changed: Added botConfigVersion plus Use latest bot settings. Refresh copies current allowed configuration, normalizes project/model/knowledge, and preserves message history.
findings.acceptance: A revision-2 conversation remains revision 2 after the bot becomes revision 3; explicit refresh updates future configuration without changing saved message IDs.

findings.expected: Deleting a project removes stale active project assignments from chats, files and bots.
findings.changed: A shared deleteProject operation unlinks related records and stamps bot/chat revisions; associated notes remain historical records but orphan scope cannot retrieve them.
findings.acceptance: Delete a project used by a bot and chat: both project IDs become null; a stale chat object cannot retrieve that project’s note.

findings.expected: Copied bot knowledge and saved-memory state have separate truthful explanations.
findings.changed: Composer copy reflects the actual memoryChoice instead of saying Saved memory stays off unconditionally. Bot knowledge remains explicitly disclosed.
remaining: Memory Off context behavior and explicit bot refresh are tested; exact composer wording is source-reviewed.
findings.acceptance: A bot chat with Memory On and copied knowledge reports memory on; with Memory Off it may send the copied note but retrieves no saved memory.

findings.expected: Multiple unresolved operations remain independently discoverable and actionable.
findings.changed: Added a bounded normalized Recovery inbox with stable IDs, open/resolved/dismissed state, context and operation metadata; resolving one does not erase another.
findings.acceptance: Persist two failures, reload/normalize, resolve one: the second stays open and visible.

findings.expected: An unrelated send may clear a transient banner without erasing unresolved recovery state.
findings.changed: Persistent recovery records outlive the transient failure banner and unrelated chat creation; alerts derive attention from both.
findings.acceptance: Create an unresolved recovery, begin unrelated work, then reload: the recovery remains open until explicitly resolved or dismissed.

findings.expected: Reload recovery uses structured operation descriptors and revalidates current context before any dispatch.
findings.changed: Persisted Notion descriptors reconstruct verification of the same operation. Other records reopen their feature/activity for review; executable callbacks are never serialized or silently replayed.
remaining: Feature-specific executable recovery beyond implemented Notion is deliberately not inferred from arbitrary recorded action strings.
findings.acceptance: Reload accepted/uncertain Notion recovery and check the same operation with confirmed:false; a workspace mismatch blocks the call and generic records never repeat external actions automatically.

findings.expected: Pending approvals remain visible independently of avatar activity or another warning.
findings.changed: Alerts contain independent pending-run approval count and Recovery entries; No current warnings excludes pending approvals/recoveries.
remaining: Alert rendering is source-reviewed; approval policy and multiple-recovery state are fixture-tested.
findings.acceptance: With two waiting approvals and an unrelated failure, Alerts still shows both approval awareness and independent recoveries.

findings.expected: Older archives do not overwrite a newer bot configuration.
findings.changed: Archive merges compare explicit update/version metadata and preserve the current record when incoming freshness is unproven.
findings.acceptance: Merge revision 1 into revision 3: current instructions, model and identity remain revision 3.

findings.expected: Restoring data cannot silently restore an old enabled schedule or grant automatic execution authority.
findings.changed: Merge is conservative about enabled state; explicit replacement disables imported schedules, and stale scheduling result state cannot redirect execution.
findings.acceptance: Merge or replace an older enabled schedule over a disabled current schedule: it does not execute until explicitly enabled again.

findings.expected: Stale imported runs cannot replace newer terminal execution state or revive old approvals.
findings.changed: Current run IDs take precedence; imported unfinished runs are paused and stripped of leases and execution approvals during restoration.
findings.acceptance: A completed local run stays completed when merged with an older queued copy; a new imported running record becomes paused without approval tokens.

findings.expected: Conversation metadata has independent revision evidence while messages and retrieval history merge safely.
findings.changed: Metadata edits receive updatedAt; merge selects the fresher metadata independently from message content and unions retrieval evidence.
findings.acceptance: A newer title/settings edit survives merging an older conversation whose message content overlaps; message IDs and conservative temporary privacy remain intact.

findings.expected: Divergent saved-memory revisions preserve the losing branch as history.
findings.changed: Merged memory history unions version entries and both differing current texts, deduplicates them and sorts deterministically while selecting the newest effective text.
findings.acceptance: Merge divergent left/right notes: newest text becomes effective and the losing text plus common base remain in version history.

findings.expected: Archive checksum validation is described as content integrity, not author/account authenticity.
findings.changed: Export manifest explicitly records authenticity=not-established and UI explains the checksum boundary; restoration revalidates execution authority.
remaining: Authenticated cross-account backup provenance/signing was not added; choosing and operating that trust model remains separate.
findings.acceptance: Export/import a synthetic archive: manifest cannot claim trusted authorship, and old schedules/approvals cannot authorize new execution.

findings.expected: Storage statistics do not serialize the full workspace while Settings is hidden.
findings.changed: The memoized Blob/JSON calculation is gated by view===settings.
remaining: No wall-clock performance gain or device benchmark is claimed.
findings.acceptance: Execute the actual storedBytes initializer in Chat: zero serialization calls. Switch to Settings: one current serialization occurs.

findings.expected: Elapsed tool timers update their own display instead of the complete CommandApp timer state.
findings.changed: Moved the 250 ms elapsed state/interval into ToolElapsed and removed timelineTickMs from CommandApp.
remaining: Component isolation is source-confirmed and elapsed calculations have existing unit coverage. React Profiler measurements of render-count/latency improvement remain unrun.
findings.acceptance: An active tool timer updates its own elapsed display, stops its interval when ended, and does not require a CommandApp-wide timer state update.

findings.expected: A seconds display checks elapsed time at second precision and derives it from the recorder clock.
findings.changed: Recording display interval is 1000 ms and derives elapsed seconds from taskRecorder.elapsed().
remaining: No device-level recording/timer accuracy claim is made.
findings.acceptance: The actual recording effect installs a 1000 ms timer; an elapsed timestamp of 2300 ms displays 2 seconds.

findings.expected: Shared dialogs have one named modal semantic, native focus containment, cancellation and opener restoration.
findings.changed: Replaced contradictory wrapper semantics with a portal-mounted native dialog, labelledBy/onDismiss at every overlay call site, showModal/close lifecycle and connected-opener restoration.
remaining: Physical keyboard, screen-reader and browser top-layer verification remain release-preview checks.
findings.acceptance: The actual Overlay fixture opens a named native dialog, handles cancel once, closes, and restores focus; all call sites supply a name and dismissal handler.

findings.expected: Shared dialogs have one named modal semantic, native focus containment, cancellation and opener restoration.
findings.changed: Replaced contradictory wrapper semantics with a portal-mounted native dialog, labelledBy/onDismiss at every overlay call site, showModal/close lifecycle and connected-opener restoration.
remaining: Physical keyboard, screen-reader and browser top-layer verification remain release-preview checks.
findings.acceptance: The actual Overlay fixture opens a named native dialog, handles cancel once, closes, and restores focus; all call sites supply a name and dismissal handler.

findings.expected: Pinning is visible and keyboard accessible without a long-press gesture.
findings.changed: Added explicit labelled Pin/Unpin controls that use the existing real pin mutation and report capacity accurately.
findings.acceptance: Activate the real Pin button: one saved pin; activate Unpin: removal; with 24 existing pins, no extra pin and a truthful limit notice.

findings.expected: Shortcut guidance matches the current platform.
findings.changed: Platform-aware shortcut helper supplies Command-K on Apple platforms and Ctrl K elsewhere after mount.
findings.acceptance: MacIntel returns Command-K and Win32 returns Ctrl K; existing shortcut handler still accepts the matching modifier.

findings.expected: Mobile navigation shares the application theme tokens while preserving reduced-motion and focus behavior.
findings.changed: Drawer background/text/radius/shadow derive from shared CSS tokens instead of separate hardcoded light/dark colors.
remaining: Token wiring is source-reviewed; a real mobile light/dark/high-contrast screenshot and focus check remain unrun. No visual-release proof is claimed.
findings.acceptance: In a controlled browser, change theme while opening the mobile drawer: shared panel/foreground tokens apply, reduced motion stays honored, and drawer focus still works.

findings.expected: Always-apply preferences cannot consume every slot needed by relevant task evidence.
findings.changed: Reserves up to four of the twelve selected slots for task-relevant non-preference notes while retaining remaining preferences.
findings.acceptance: With twelve preferences and one relevant budget note, the result stays within twelve and includes the budget evidence.

findings.expected: A free local path recognizes bounded common equivalent terms without claiming full semantic understanding.
findings.changed: Canonicalized a small explicit cost/deadline/task/project/preference vocabulary before lexical scoring; no embedding or paid retrieval call introduced.
remaining: Full semantic/entity/recency hybrid retrieval from the original architectural proposal remains unimplemented and needs a separate storage/privacy/cost design.
findings.acceptance: A question using pricing retrieves a note using budget; unrelated notes do not acquire fabricated semantic evidence.

findings.expected: Quoting a conversation carries an identified useful excerpt instead of only its first user message.
findings.changed: Quotes a bounded recent exchange with role labels and an explicit shortening notice; helper also supports a selected message identity.
findings.acceptance: Quote a completed exchange: its recent assistant reply is included and shortened excerpts are disclosed, preserving a link to the source identity.

findings.expected: A quoted task preserves applicable custom conversation instructions and explicit copied bot context.
findings.changed: Carries customPersonality, bot knowledge/provider/tier and source lineage into the new task while retaining its own chat identity.
findings.acceptance: Quote a custom two-paragraph style conversation: the new task keeps that style and source lineage without altering the original.

findings.expected: Editing produces a revised branch while preserving the original conversation.
findings.changed: At the inspected base, CommandApp already created a new edited branch and retained wsRef.current.chats. Added helper-level archived-original preservation so direct reviseUserTurn callers are also non-destructive.
remaining: Historical claim is narrowed: the production UI caller was already branching at the base revision. The new change is defensive helper behavior, not proof of a previously destructive UI path.
findings.acceptance: Edit an earlier user turn: revised branch excludes obsolete answers while the original message sequence remains recoverable; direct helper calls also preserve an archived original.

findings.expected: Standalone conversation exports carry configuration and explicitly state attachment portability limits.
findings.changed: Export includes chat configuration, IDs, source image metadata and clear inline/blob/remote-media coverage wording.
findings.acceptance: Export a custom-style bot conversation with images: configuration and inline bytes remain available; blob-only/external-media references are disclosed as incomplete portable media.

findings.expected: Pre-dispatch context sizing should include selected-model capacity, output reservation and modality/tool overhead.

findings.expected: Local knowledge search preserves record identity, source, revision and scope.
findings.changed: LocalResult contains structured records; search text includes stable note ID, scope, source and updated time rather than only concatenated content.
findings.acceptance: Search a synthetic note: structured result returns its exact ID/source/time/scope and does not infer unprovided provenance.

findings.expected: Conflicting saved records remain distinguishable without presenting an unverified merged truth.
findings.changed: Returns separate sourced records and explicitly says multiple records’ disagreement has not been resolved.
remaining: Automatic conflict detection/adjudication, authority ranking and entity reconciliation remain a larger knowledge-policy proposal. The patch does not claim that an unresolved conflict has been resolved.
findings.acceptance: Return two disagreeing notes as separate identified records with an unresolved-evidence notice. Future adjudication must preserve both sources and expose the chosen authority/uncertainty policy.

findings.expected: Projects with the same display name remain distinguishable in local discovery.
findings.changed: Project records and human-readable discovery output include stable project IDs and descriptions.
findings.acceptance: List same-name projects and receive distinct project IDs without choosing a destination solely by name.

findings.expected: Global search supports independent query terms and deliberate quoted phrases.
findings.changed: Tokenized ordinary terms match independently; quoted groups remain contiguous phrase constraints.
findings.acceptance: launch budget matches Budget is ready for the launch; the quoted phrase "launch budget" does not match that reversed separated wording.

findings.expected: Global search ranks exact/prefix titles above incidental body matches deterministically.
findings.changed: Adds title exact/prefix/term scores with stable tie-breaks and a small archived penalty.
findings.acceptance: An exact Launch Budget title ranks above matching older body messages; ties produce a stable order.

findings.expected: A conversation can expose each matching message and navigate to its exact location.
findings.changed: Search results include messageId and excerpt per matching message; navigation focuses the identified message with an accessible focus outline.
remaining: Actual browser scrolling/focus visibility remains a preview check.
findings.acceptance: Two matching messages in one chat produce two distinct message IDs; choosing one targets that message rather than always the first match.

findings.expected: Search results clearly distinguish archived and temporary conversations.
findings.changed: Result metadata carries archived/temporary indicators rather than implying they are ordinary active chats; private local data is not exported to a search service.
findings.acceptance: A matching archived temporary chat visibly identifies both states; choosing it does not silently unarchive it or alter its privacy mode.

findings.expected: Search results include project context and support project-name discovery.
findings.changed: Resolves project names for chat/file result metadata and query matching while retaining stable project IDs.
findings.acceptance: Search North: matching project-scoped chats appear with North context and distinct identities even when titles are identical.

findings.expected: Custom personality limits are disclosed and imported truncation remains visible.
findings.changed: Added effective-length/limit status, persistent imported truncation flag and Settings notice; explicit edits can clear the warning after correction.
findings.acceptance: Normalize an oversized imported style: the 800-character limit is disclosed and its warning survives reopen until corrected.

findings.expected: Custom instruction paragraphs and line structure survive safe normalization.
findings.changed: Normalizes control characters/horizontal spacing without flattening newlines; two-paragraph spacing survives prompt construction.
findings.acceptance: Two paragraphs remain two paragraphs in normalized custom style and the generated personality instruction.

findings.expected: Unavailable personality IDs use an explicit safe fallback with a persistent explanation.
findings.changed: Unknown IDs record personalityFallback and use Assistant; default-style load warns, imported warnings survive normalization, and a valid explicit choice clears fallback.
findings.acceptance: Import retired-style: Assistant is effective, retired-style remains visible as the fallback reason, reopen preserves it, and choosing Custom clears it.
